Wikipedia is explicitly cited despite task instructions forbidding it; raw launch tables are pasted directly with orphan superscript tags; figures lack formal numbering and captions; reference [10] is corrupted; the bibliography consists only of bare URLs; and an incomplete sentence is left in the EOL section.

technical_issues.issue: Kourou (Guiana Space Centre) latitude is stated as 45.05°N; French Guiana is located near equatorial latitudes (~5.2°N).
A 600 km circular sun-synchronous orbit requires a retrograde inclination of ~97.8°. The reported value of 87.79° is prograde and physically non-sun-synchronous.
The STK report lists a mean contact duration of 580.786 s (9.68 minutes), which the text erroneously claims is 'almost twenty minutes'.
The final sentence of the section cuts off abruptly mid-clause ('utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable').

overall: The report presents a commendable concept for Australian coral reef observation supported by STK simulations. However, it suffers from several critical engineering errors (prograde SSO inclination, misplaced launch site latitude, flawed time conversion) and poor presentation, notably bare URLs, incomplete sentences, and direct reliance on prohibited Wikipedia sources.
